rules.title: Edge is computed from a recorded probability and a recorded price
rules.description: The recorded edge equals the estimated fair probability minus the probability implied by the offered price.
rules.rationale: Edge is the quantity the whole pipeline exists to produce, and it is a comparison between a belief and a price. Recording it without both inputs makes it an assertion.
rules.remediation: Recompute the edge from the recorded fair probability and the recorded implied probability.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that the edge follows from its recorded inputs. It says nothing about whether those inputs are right.

rules.title: A minimum edge is defined in policy
rules.description: The betting policy defines the minimum edge, after the uncertainty discount, that a BET requires.
rules.rationale: A threshold decided case by case is not a threshold. Fixing it in configuration is what makes it possible to say afterwards whether a decision respected it.
rules.remediation: Set minEdge in betting-policy.yml, at a level that exceeds what transaction costs and estimation error consume.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that a threshold exists and is well-formed. Whether it is set high enough is a judgement no check can make.

rules.title: No BET is placed below the minimum edge
rules.description: Every BET record shows an edge, after the uncertainty discount, at or above the policy minimum. A tie meets the threshold.
rules.rationale: The threshold is where the pack's caution lives. An edge below it is inside the error bar of the estimate that produced it, and betting it is betting on noise.
rules.remediation: Record the decision as a PASS. A PASS below the threshold is the system working, not an opportunity missed.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance over recorded decisions, scoped to the recorded universe. A wager placed and never recorded is invisible here.

rules.title: No wager is placed only because an outcome is likely
rules.description: A high probability of winning is not a reason to wager. Every decision passes through the offered price, and the quantity that justifies a BET is edge, never probability alone.
rules.rationale: This is the most common losing bet there is: the favourite really is likely to win, and the price already says so, and often says so generously. Backing likely winners at any price is a reliable way to lose money slowly while being right most of the time.
rules.remediation: Compute the edge against the offered price. If the price already reflects the probability, the correct decision is PASS.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a price entered the pipeline and that the edge was computed against it. It cannot establish the bettor's motive — a record can show the arithmetic was done and still describe a decision that was really made because the team looked good.

rules.title: Edge is never fabricated
rules.description: No edge is stated that does not follow from a recorded probability and a recorded price. A stated edge that does not recompute is a fabrication, not a rounding difference.
rules.rationale: Edge is the number that authorises risking money. Stating one that does not follow from its inputs is the shortest path from a wish to a wager.
rules.remediation: Recompute the edge from the recorded inputs, or correct the inputs to the values actually used.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects an edge inconsistent with its recorded inputs. An edge computed correctly from a fabricated probability or price passes this check and is caught, if at all, by the provenance rules.
